newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on Korea tension fears.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on Korea tension fears.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed sharply lower on Wednesday as jittery investors dumped their shares on the news that North Korea had issued a stern warning of war to the United States and South Korea, brokers said.

They said an unstable money market combined with recent increases in interest rates also pressured investor sentiment. Kia Group shares remained weak throughout the day on investor concerns about financial problems in the group, even though the group strongly denied the market rumours.
The composite stock index lost 19.08 points, or 2.41 percent, to 773.21, off the day's high of 799.54.
"As the index rises to a peak without proper consolidation, investors tend to take their profits in a hurry whenever there is a negative news," said Kim Myong-ho at Hyundai Securities.
"They used the North Korean issue as an excuse for a downward correction," said Cha Hee-gun at Sunkyong Securities.
North Korea warned it was ready for a "final battle" with the U.S. and South Korea, which it accused of preparing to attack while the North was weakened by a dire food shortage.
The threat used language that was strong even by the strident standards of North's daily anti-South propaganda, analysts said.
But the South Korean military denied stepping up military exercises and Seoul officials accused North Korea of trying to justify its huge military spendings by whipping up war threats.

"Foreign investors are worrying about growing country risk with the news and began selling their holdings," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities. "The sell-off deepened falls in the market, which was about to consolidate."
"As the market over-reacted to the North Korean issue, the consolidation will not be too big," said Kim of Hyundai.
Brokers said investors were concerned about recent rises in overnight call rates.
